cadence_words: One round a month. Each round is written to the public record before the month opens, and closes for each entrant when that entrant's 60th graded forecast lands, which for the slower entrants can take months. Nothing is graded early, and no entrant-round is ever graded on fewer than the full 60.

error_words: The one measure, the same for everyone: over an entrant's next 60 graded forecasts, take how often the event actually happened, subtract the average of what the entrant said, and read the difference in points. Above zero means the entrant understated how often its event happens (its band held more often than promised, or its chances ran low). Below zero means it overstated. Zero is a perfectly honest forecaster.

explanation.body: Its forecast takes this form: distribution, over next 60 graded forecasts per entrant, monthly. It is graded on how often its stated ranges contain what actually happens, checked against the width of those ranges. It would be ended if after 12 monthly rounds, its interval hit rate is no better than a no-change forecast of each entrant's trailing error. It counts as proven at 12 monthly rounds.
explanation.summary: Predict, a month ahead, how far each forecaster's stated confidence is about to miss what actually happens, and be graded on the prediction.

how_words: Each coming range is built from the entrant's own measured record so far: its running error, the count behind it, and any built-in tilt an earlier study measured in its construction, carried forward with the width that plain chance over just 60 forecasts honestly needs. That is why the ranges are wide: 60 forecasts is a small sample, and a narrower range would be pretending to know more than the record holds.
idea_words: Every forecaster on this site states a confidence: a band that promises to hold 68 times in 100, a chance of reaching a level, a range that promises 80 in 100. This page is a league that predicts, one month ahead, how far each of those promises is about to miss over its next 60 graded forecasts, and stakes its own record on the prediction. Its ranges and its ranking are written to the same public record before the month opens, and graded by the same rule when the 60 forecasts land. A league that grades everyone else's honesty is itself graded, in public, on whether it called the honesty right.
kill_words: After 12 monthly rounds, if the share of this league's ranges that contained the real error is no better than a no-change rival, one that simply carries each entrant's latest measured error forward with the same width, this page retires and its record stays up intact. Both hit rates and both widths are published at each round's close, so a win on width alone would show.

live_record.words: 1 round(s) issued and 8 league forecasts on record; 0 graded so far. A round grades only when an entrant's full 60 forecasts have been graded, so early rounds stay open for months. Twelve monthly rounds decide whether it stands or retires.

proof_gate.words: The proof gate scanned 15815 names and wrote each name's provisional state to the forward record, where it will be checked against what the name does next. Every state is provisional: 13973 names read MIXED, 1842 are still OBSERVING, and 0 names are SUPPORTED today, so no name on this page is shown as proven. 15834 names carry an earlier superseded row from the first partial scan beside their current one; the record is append only, both rows stay on it, and every count on this page counts each name once.

ranking_words: Entrants are ranked by how small their coming error is predicted to be. Because several entrants are built the same way, the headline ranking groups them by kind and counts each kind once, at the middle of its members: four forecasters built from movement and spread agreeing is one voice, not four.
